cases.question: What did Nitin work on at BNY?
cases.answer: Nitin worked as a Java Software Engineer at BNY from August 2024 to September 2024, in a remote contract role based in Frisco, TX [experience-bny#1]. He enhanced Java and Spring Boot services for data-ingestion, validation and processing workflows on the Bridgewater platform [experience-bny#2]. He also implemented REST APIs for internal-system integration, built relational data-access components using JDBC and Spring Data, optimized queries and resolved defects within Agile sprints [experience-bny#3].

cases.question: What frontend technologies does Nitin know?
cases.answer: Nitin's frontend skills include React, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3 and JSP, along with integrating front ends with REST APIs and microservices [skills#4]. In his Copart role as a Java Full Stack Engineer, he developed reusable React single-page application components using JavaScript, HTML5 and CSS3, integrated with backend REST APIs for auction and inventory workflows [experience-copart#3].

cases.question: Has Nitin worked with Kubernetes in production?
cases.answer: The background materials don't mention Kubernetes, so I can't confirm whether Nitin has worked with it in production. They do list AWS (including ECS), Docker and Terraform under cloud and DevOps [skills#2]. For a direct answer, contact Nitin through the Contact section of this page.

cases.question: Is Agentic Compass a personal side project or something used at work?
cases.answer: It is work, not a side project. Nitin designed and built Agentic Compass in his current role as Senior Software Engineer at MAS Global Consulting, on the JPMorganChase assignment (Offers team) [experience-jpmc-offers#7] [project-agentic-compass#1]. The sources describe it as professional work, not a personal project [project-agentic-compass#1]. It is in production after senior engineering lead reviews and UAT [project-agentic-compass#2]. His personal projects are PaymentOps Workbench and Ask Nitin, which are separate from it [profile#7].

cases.question: How does Agentic Compass decide which specialist skill handles a ticket?
cases.answer: In his current role, Nitin designed and built Agentic Compass [project-agentic-compass#1]. It uses deterministic ticket routing, with a routing table of 19 routes, including container and dependency vulnerabilities, static analysis, component testing, feature development and infrastructure-as-code, plus an unknown route [project-agentic-compass#7]. The routes reference 61 specialist skills, and all of them resolve [project-agentic-compass#7]. The router delegates domain work to these existing skills rather than duplicating them [project-agentic-compass#4]. The sources don't describe the exact matching rules beyond this.

cases.answer: Nitin's current title is Senior Software Engineer at MAS Global Consulting, working with JPMorganChase as the client on the Offers team [experience-jpmc-offers#1]. He builds Java/Spring Boot microservices and REST APIs in that role [experience-jpmc-offers#1].
